title: William V. S. Tubman Inaugurated as 18th President
reason: Tubman was inaugurated as Liberia's 18th president on January 3, 1944, after being elected in May 1943. His 27-year tenure is confirmed by multiple authoritative sources.

title: Open Door Investment Policy Launched
reason: The Open Door Policy was formally announced in 1944 upon Tubman's inauguration, inviting foreign investment to exploit natural resources. It attracted hundreds of millions of dollars in investment and is well-documented.

title: Unification Policy Extends Voting Rights to Indigenous Citizens
reason: Tubman's Unification Policy did extend political rights to indigenous Liberians, but sources give different dates (1946 or 1951) for when suffrage was formally extended; the policy's incremental implementation makes the exact year contested.

title: Firestone Rubber Plantation Dominates Liberian Economy
reason: Firestone's 99-year, one-million-acre concession signed in 1926 made it Liberia's dominant employer and export earner through the 1950s; labor conditions were widely criticized by international observers.

title: Plot Against Tubman Uncovered — Opposition Suppressed
reason: Coup plots and political repression under Tubman are well-documented; multiple sources confirm that allegations of plots were used to consolidate power and suppress opposition during his presidency.

title: LAMCO Iron Ore Concession Agreement Signed
reason: The original concession for Nimba Mountain was granted in 1953 to a US firm; Swedish partners joined in 1955 creating LAMCO. The 1956 date for the LAMCO concession agreement is not confirmed by sources, which place the key dates in 1953 and 1955.

title: Liberia Becomes Founding Member of Conference of Independent African States
reason: Liberia was one of eight independent African states that attended the founding Conference of Independent African States in Accra, Ghana, April 15-22, 1958.

title: LAMCO Iron Ore Exports Begin from Nimba
reason: LAMCO began shipping iron ore from Nimba in 1963, not 1960; the port of Buchanan opened for traffic in 1963 and production reached 2.5 million tons in its inaugural year.

title: Liberia Joins Organization of African Unity as Founding Member
reason: Liberia was among the 32 founding members of the OAU established in Addis Ababa in May 1963; Liberia signed the OAU Charter on August 29, 1963, and hosted a key pre-OAU summit in Sanniquellie in 1959.

title: First General Population Census Conducted
reason: Liberia's first national population census was conducted in 1962, not 1964; the 1962 census recorded a population of approximately 1.016 million and is confirmed by official Liberian government sources and IHSN.

title: Tubman Re-elected for Sixth Term — Consolidation of Personal Rule
reason: Tubman was re-elected for a sixth term but the election was held on May 2, 1967 (not 1966), with inauguration in January 1968; the description of uncontested True Whig rule and patronage is accurate.

title: President Tubman Dies — William Tolbert Succeeds After 27-Year Presidency
reason: William Tubman died on July 23, 1971 in a London clinic following a prostate operation; Vice President William Tolbert was constitutionally elevated to the presidency as confirmed by multiple sources.

title: Tolbert Pursues Mildly Progressive Reforms — Rhetoric of Transformation
reason: Tolbert's 'Total Involvement for Higher Heights' program is well-documented; he joined the Non-Aligned Movement and pursued reforms while his family maintained economic dominance, consistent with the description.

title: Diplomatic Relations Established with Communist China
reason: Liberia established diplomatic relations with the PRC on February 17, 1977, not 1974; the description of breaking from Taiwan and joining the Non-Aligned Movement is accurate but the year is incorrect.

title: Rice Riots Kill Dozens — Urban Discontent Explodes
reason: On April 14, 1979, protests against a rice price increase turned violent; security forces killed at least 50 protesters, Guinean troops were invited to restore order, and a state of emergency was imposed, all confirmed by multiple sources.

title: Military Coup — Doe Executes Tolbert, Ends Americo-Liberian Rule
reason: On April 12, 1980, Master Sergeant Samuel Doe and 17 noncommissioned officers seized the Executive Mansion, killed Tolbert, and publicly executed 13 cabinet ministers on a Monrovia beach ten days later, ending Americo-Liberian rule.

title: People's Redemption Council Suspends Constitution and Political Parties
reason: The PRC immediately suspended the constitution, dissolved the legislature, and banned political parties; the US quickly recognized Doe for Cold War reasons, consistent with the description.

title: Thomas Quiwonkpa Dismissed from PRC — Factional Splits Begin
reason: Quiwonkpa was dismissed but sources indicate his removal occurred in October 1983, not 1981; the description of factional splits and eventual exile is accurate.

title: New Constitution Approved by Referendum — Return to Civilian Rule Promised
reason: On July 3, 1984, a revised constitution was approved by 78.3% of voters; the new constitution established bicameral legislature and presidential elections under US pressure, entering into force January 6, 1986.

title: Fraudulent Election Hands Doe Disputed Victory
reason: The October 1985 election was documented as heavily fraudulent; Doe was declared winner with 50.9% while observers said Jackson Doe actually won; the US accepted the outcome for Cold War reasons.

title: Quiwonkpa Coup Attempt Crushed — Brutal Reprisals on Nimba County
reason: On November 12, 1985, Quiwonkpa invaded from Sierra Leone, seized Radio Monrovia briefly, was captured and killed; Doe's forces conducted brutal reprisals against Gio and Mano civilians in Nimba County, fueling later civil war recruitment.

title: First Civil War Begins — NPFL Invades from Ivory Coast
reason: Charles Taylor's NPFL crossed into Nimba County from Côte d'Ivoire on December 24, 1989, with approximately 100 fighters, rapidly recruiting Gio and Mano fighters motivated by resentment of Doe's post-1985 reprisals.

title: ECOMOG Intervention Force Deployed to Liberia
reason: ECOMOG deployed approximately 3,500 troops to Monrovia on August 24-25, 1990, led by Ghana's Lt. General Quainoo; it was the first ECOWAS military intervention and created a buffer preventing Taylor from capturing the capital.

title: President Doe Captured and Executed by INPFL Forces
reason: Samuel Doe was captured on September 9, 1990 by Prince Johnson's INPFL at ECOMOG headquarters, tortured and executed on video; the footage was widely distributed across West Africa.

title: Interim Government of National Unity Established Under Amos Sawyer
reason: ECOWAS brokered the establishment of the IGNU in Banjul; Amos Sawyer was elected president on August 29, 1990, serving from November 22, 1990 to March 7, 1994.

title: Operation Octopus — Taylor Attacks Monrovia, ECOMOG Repulses Assault
reason: Operation Octopus launched October 15, 1992; NPFL advanced into Monrovia's outskirts, killed an estimated 3,000 civilians and fighters, but was repulsed by combined ECOMOG, AFL, and ULIMO forces.

title: Cotonou Peace Agreement Signed — First Major Peace Deal
reason: The Cotonou Peace Agreement was signed July 25, 1993 by the NPFL, ULIMO, and IGNU; UNOMIL was established by the Security Council on September 22, 1993 to assist ECOMOG in implementation.

title: Proliferation of Armed Factions — Seven Groups Fighting Simultaneously
reason: By 1994 the conflict involved NPFL, ULIMO-K, ULIMO-J (split in 1994), LPC, AFL remnants, LDF, and ECOMOG; child soldiers, looting, and aid diversion were widely documented.

title: Abuja Peace Agreement Provides New Framework for Transition
reason: The Abuja Accord was signed August 19, 1995 and was confirmed to be the thirteenth peace deal since the war began in 1989; it established a Council of State including Taylor as member.

title: April 6 War — Final Major Urban Battle Devastates Monrovia
reason: Factional fighting erupted April 6, 1996 as NPFL and ULIMO-K targeted ULIMO-J leader Roosevelt Johnson; approximately 1,000 civilians were killed, Monrovia was looted, and hundreds of thousands fled.

title: Charles Taylor Wins Presidential Election — 'He Killed My Ma, He Killed My Pa, I Will Vote For Him'
reason: Taylor won the July 19, 1997 election with 75.3% of the vote; the slogan reflecting fear-driven voting is widely documented, and international observers declared the election broadly credible.

title: Taylor Government Accused of Sponsoring Sierra Leone's RUF
reason: UN investigators and journalists produced extensive evidence of Taylor supplying the RUF with weapons in exchange for conflict diamonds; the Special Court later confirmed this in its 2012 conviction.

title: LURD Rebel Movement Launches Second Civil War from Guinea
reason: LURD was organized in July 1999 and launched incursions from Guinea from 1999-2000; Guinea backed LURD in retaliation for Taylor's support of Guinean rebels, confirmed by multiple sources.

title: UN Security Council Imposes Sanctions on Liberia
reason: UNSC Resolution 1343 was adopted March 7, 2001 (not 2000), imposing an arms embargo, diamond embargo, and travel bans on Liberian officials in response to RUF support; the year in the event is one year early.

title: Movement for Democracy in Liberia Opens Southern Front
reason: MODEL was formed in September 2002 and crossed into southern Liberia in March 2003, not 2001; it was backed by Côte d'Ivoire as retaliation for Taylor supporting Ivorian rebels.

title: Special Court for Sierra Leone Indicts Taylor for War Crimes
reason: The indictment was approved March 7, 2003 and unsealed June 4, 2003 while Taylor attended peace talks in Accra, Ghana; he returned to Liberia and rejected the indictment.

title: LURD Forces Besiege Monrovia — Humanitarian Catastrophe
reason: LURD besieged Monrovia July 18 - August 14, 2003, killing around 1,000 civilians; shells struck the US embassy and hundreds of thousands of internally displaced persons concentrated in the capital.

title: Accra Comprehensive Peace Agreement — Taylor Exiled to Nigeria
reason: The Accra Comprehensive Peace Agreement was signed August 18, 2003; Taylor resigned and left for Calabar, Nigeria on August 11, 2003, offered asylum by President Obasanjo.

title: UNMIL Peacekeeping Mission Deployed — Largest UN Mission in Africa
reason: UNMIL was authorized by UNSC Resolution 1509 on September 19, 2003, deploying up to 15,000 military personnel; it took over from ECOMOG on October 1, 2003 and oversaw disarmament of approximately 103,000 combatants.

title: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf Elected — First Female Head of State in Africa
reason: Sirleaf won the presidential runoff on November 8, 2005 with 59.4% of the vote, defeating George Weah; she became Africa's first democratically elected female head of state and took office January 16, 2006.

title: Truth and Reconciliation Commission Established
reason: The TRC began officially operating on February 22, 2006, with a mandate covering January 1979 to October 2003; its final report was released July 1, 2009, recommending prosecution of dozens including some current officials.

title: Charles Taylor Transferred to Special Court for Sierra Leone
reason: Taylor was arrested in Nigeria on March 29, 2006 and transferred to the Special Court for Sierra Leone, then relocated to The Hague on June 20, 2006 for security reasons; he was the first sitting head of state transferred to an international tribunal.

title: Sirleaf Government Cancels Corrupt Concessions — Natural Resource Governance Reform
reason: The Sirleaf government reviewed and renegotiated concession agreements, including the ArcelorMittal MDA ratified in May 2007; sources confirm renegotiation and cancellation of some contracts but the ArcelorMittal agreement was renegotiated rather than cancelled.

title: Global Financial Crisis Collapses Iron Ore and Rubber Revenues
reason: The 2008-09 global financial crisis caused sharp declines in commodity prices for iron ore and rubber, Liberia's primary exports; the IMF and World Bank provided emergency support to prevent fiscal collapse.

title: HIPC Debt Relief — Liberia's $4.9 Billion Debt Cancelled
reason: Liberia reached the HIPC completion point on June 29, 2010, but the actual relief granted was $4.6 billion (not $4.9 billion); the event correctly notes the debt stock before relief was $4.9 billion but conflates debt stock with amount cancelled.

title: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf Awarded Nobel Peace Prize
reason: Sirleaf was awarded the 2011 Nobel Peace Prize jointly with Leymah Gbowee and Tawakkol Karman 'for their non-violent struggle for the safety of women and for women's rights to full participation in peace-building work.'

title: Charles Taylor Convicted of War Crimes and Crimes Against Humanity
reason: Taylor was convicted on April 26, 2012 and sentenced on May 30, 2012, not in 2011; the conviction on all 11 counts is accurate in substance but the year assigned in this event is incorrect.

title: Sirleaf Re-elected in Presidential Runoff
reason: Sirleaf won the November 2011 runoff with 90.7% after opposition candidate Winston Tubman of the Congress for Democratic Change boycotted the second round alleging fraud; international observers endorsed the process.

title: Ebola Epidemic Declared — Worst Outbreak in History Hits Liberia
reason: Liberia became the epicenter of the worst Ebola outbreak in history from 2014-2016; Monrovia hospitals were overwhelmed by July 2014, health workers died at high rates, and Liberia recorded the highest death toll of any country at approximately 4,800.

title: State of Emergency Declared — Schools and Borders Closed
reason: Sirleaf declared a 90-day state of emergency on August 6, 2014; schools were closed on July 30, 2014; the West Point slum quarantine provoked violent protests; GDP growth collapsed from over 8% to near zero.

title: International Military Response — US Deploys 3,000 Troops to Build Ebola Treatment Centers
reason: Obama authorized deployment of approximately 3,000 military personnel to Liberia in September 2014 under Operation United Assistance to construct Ebola treatment units and train health workers; the deployment catalyzed broader international contributions.

title: Liberia Declared Ebola-Free — Approximately 5,000 Dead
reason: WHO declared Liberia free of Ebola transmission on May 9, 2015; confirmed deaths reached approximately 4,716-4,800; over 380 health workers died; two subsequent flares were contained before final declaration in January 2016.

title: Ebola Leaves Economic Devastation — GDP Contracts
reason: GDP growth fell sharply during the epidemic but did not fully contract to negative; the World Bank revised 2014 growth to 2.2% (from 5.9%) with slow recovery in 2015; poverty increased significantly but the 10-13% poverty increase figure needs further sourcing.

title: UNMIL Peacekeeping Mission Begins Drawdown
reason: UNMIL completed transfer of security responsibilities to Liberian authorities on June 30, 2016; the mission formally closed in March 2018 after nearly 15 years, transferring full security responsibility to the Liberia National Police and AFL.

title: George Weah Wins Presidential Election — Peaceful Transfer of Power
reason: Weah won the December 26, 2017 presidential runoff with approximately 60% of the vote, defeating Vice President Boakai; Sirleaf's acceptance of results and Weah's January 2018 inauguration marked Liberia's first peaceful democratic transfer of power since independence.

title: Weah Government Inherits Severe Economic Challenges
reason: Weah took office amid a depreciating Liberian dollar (down 25% in 2017 and further in 2018), inflation exceeding 24%, a $225 million fiscal deficit, collapse of UNMIL hard currency inflows, and low commodity prices.

title: L$16 Billion Missing Cash Scandal Rocks Weah Administration
reason: In 2018, approximately L$16 billion in newly printed banknotes could not be accounted for; a Kroll audit found irregularities including excess printing; multiple officials including Charles Sirleaf were charged and later released.

title: Massive Anti-Government Protest Draws Tens of Thousands
reason: The major 'Save the State' protest organized by the Council of Patriots occurred on June 7, 2019, not January 7, 2019; the description of demands for accountability and its scale as one of Liberia's largest protests is accurate.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Hits Liberia — Health System Under Renewed Pressure
reason: Liberia confirmed its first COVID-19 cases on March 16, 2020; the government declared a state of emergency on April 8, 2020; Ebola-derived contact tracing infrastructure provided institutional advantage, and official mortality remained relatively low.

title: Liberia Launches National Road Development Projects
reason: The Weah administration prioritized road construction financed through World Bank loans and Chinese bilateral funding; road projects were a central plank of the Pro-Poor Agenda for Prosperity and Development and generated employment.

title: Weah Administration Faces Persistent Inflation and Currency Crisis
reason: Liberia experienced sustained inflation and Liberian dollar depreciation through 2022, driven by high fuel import costs and global commodity price shocks following the Ukraine war; economic difficulties significantly eroded public support for Weah.

title: Joseph Boakai Defeats Weah in Presidential Runoff — Second Peaceful Transfer of Power
reason: Boakai defeated Weah in the November 14, 2023 runoff with 50.64% of the vote; Weah conceded before final results were announced, enabling Liberia's second consecutive peaceful democratic transition.

title: Boakai Inaugurated — Pledges Anti-Corruption Drive and Economic Recovery
reason: Joseph Boakai was sworn in as Liberia's 25th president on January 22, 2024, pledging anti-corruption as top priority; he suspended over 450 officials for non-compliance with asset declaration rules and cut his own salary by 40%.

title: War and Economic Crimes Court Establishment Launched Under Boakai
reason: President Boakai signed an executive order establishing the War and Economic Crimes Court on May 2, 2024, fulfilling a 2009 TRC recommendation; subsequent legislative endorsement occurred in March 2024, though full permanent legislation is still pending.
